faqs.answer:
The best place to start is the **New to CDU** page. It walks you through activating your account, enrolling, setting up IT and getting your timetable.

If you'd like one-on-one help with account activation, enrolment, study plans or timetables, visit the support staff in the **Library Foyer** (ITMS, Student Central and Library staff are based there).

faqs.question: How do I activate my student account?
faqs.answer:

faqs.question: How do I apply for a USI?
faqs.answer:
Getting a **Unique Student Identifier (USI)** is quick, easy and free.

1. Have a valid form of ID ready.
2. Create your USI on the USI Registry System.
3. Enter your USI in **My Student Info**, under Enrolment Steps.

Your USI is needed for CDU's government reporting, and for international students it also matters for visa compliance.

faqs.question: I have a driver's licence. Can I drive in the Northern Territory?
faqs.answer:

- If your licence isn't in English, you need an **International Driving Permit**, or an official English translation from an authorised translator in the NT. Carry it with your licence whenever you drive.
- If you stay in the NT **for more than 3 months**, you must transfer to an **NT driver licence**.

faqs.question: How many units do I need to enrol in to keep my Global Merit Scholarship?

faqs.question: If I fail a unit, do I lose my scholarship?
faqs.answer:

- After a first fail, plan how to repeat the unit or find another pathway, especially if it's a core unit.
- Repeated fails can lead to an Under Review or Under Progression notice. If you're contacted by the Progression team, **respond and follow their guidance**.
- You may lose eligibility if you don't show improvement or don't tell CDU Global your plans.

faqs.question: How can I transfer my EndNote Library to another computer?
faqs.answer:
To move your EndNote Library to another location, you need to first compress the original EndNote Library or Groups of the Library you want to move.
1. Compress your EndNote Library file:
Open the EndNote Library.
Go to File and select Compressed Library (.enlx).
In the dialogue box that appears, you can choose to either Create or Create & Email.
Select whether to create With File Attachments or Without File attachments.
Click Next (Windows) or OK (Mac) and save it at your desired location.
2. Move the compressed file to the second computer:
Option 1: Email the zip file to yourself.
Option 2: Use cloud storage service such as OneDrive if the zip file is too big to email.
Option 3: Transport the zip file using a flash drive.

faqs.question: How do I create a Hanging Indent?
faqs.answer:
According to Business Dictionary (n.d.), a hanging indent is a "style of paragraph composing in which the first line of a text is aligned with the left margin, and all other lines are indented (moved toward right) by an equal amount of space".
The APA reference style uses hanging indents in the references. The hanging indent is 5-7 spaces (1.27cm in a Word document).
For example:
Roitman, J. L., & La Fontaine, T. P. (2012). The exercise professional’s guide to optimizing health: Strategies for
preventing and reducing chronic disease. Wolters Kluwer Health.
There are various ways to create a hanging indent for APA referencing.

faqs.answer:

It is often different to the URL that appears at the top of your browser - the link displayed there maybe session dependent, and may not work reliably.
To ensure a link is reliable, you will need to locate the permanent link to the article or create a permalink.

Is EndNote telling you to insert a citation, every time you have text in a bracket/parenthesis in your text? This happens when the temporary citation delimiters for EndNote are improperly set to parenthesis. Follow these steps to change the settings:
If you are using Windows:
1. Open your document and go to the EndNote toolbar.

3. Check your "Temporary citation delimiters." If these are set to ( and ), this explains your issue. By setting this, you have told EndNote that everything it sees enclosed within ( and ) is a citation. Change these back to the default, { and }, and then click OK.

faqs.question: What is a DOI and where can I find it?
faqs.answer:
DOI stands for Digital Object Identifier. It is a unique address for an online resource, just like a URL.
Many electronic resources (esp. journal articles) have a DOI. The location of the DOI may vary depending on the type of database you are using, however you can usually find the DOI on the first page of the article or database. See below for some examples:
In APA 7th ensure you format your DOI this way (incl. hyperlink): https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mnl.2011.07.013
If the DOI on your resource shows in the old format, as in the examples above, change the DOI as follows:
Old DOI format: DOI:10.1016/j.mnl.2011.07.013
New DOI format: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mnl.2011.07.013 (removing 'DOI:' and replacing it with 'https://doi.org/').

faqs.question: Why can't I access an eBook?
faqs.answer:
The library subscribes to a range of electronic books from different publishers. Some of these have restrictive license conditions i.e., 3 user access models
This means only 3 people can access the title concurrently, whether to download or read online. There is usually a 30-minute inactivity setting built in so that if there is no activity with the book in that time, you will be logged out, and the license becomes available for another client. The Library will buy multi-user licenses wherever possible.
For other troubleshooting tips to issues accessing the eBooks, see the eBook Guide.

faqs.question: Why are my EndNote references in a strange font or spacing?
faqs.answer:
You can change the font and spacing for EndNote Citations using the EndNote ribbon in Word.
For Windows:
1. Open Microsoft Word and click on the EndNote 20 tab.
2. Click on the small arrow in the corner of the bibliography section. This will open a box to configure the settings.
3. Click on the 'Layout' tab.
4. Adjust the font and line spacing to match your document.
For Mac:
1. Open Microsoft Word and click on the EndNote 20 tab.
2. Click on 'Configure Bibliography'. This will open a box to configure the settings.
3. Click on the 'Layout' tab.
4. Adjust the font and line spacing to match your document.

faqs.question: I get an error installing EndNote on my Mac. What do I do?
faqs.answer:
Before installing EndNote on your Mac, you must close EndNote and any Microsoft Office (Word, Powerpoint etc.) products that are running.
To close an app on your Mac normally, choose Quit from the app's menu in the menu bar. Or press Command-Q.
If the app won't close, follow these steps to force the app to close.
Do either of the following:
Press these three keys together: Option, Command, Esc (Escape).
Or choose Force Quit from the Apple menu  in the corner of your screen.
A Force Quit window will open. Select the app that you want to close, then click Force Quit.
Retry the EndNote installation process.

faqs.question: How do I back up my library in EndNote?
faqs.answer:
To back up your library in EndNote, there are two options:
Option One
To use the 'Save a Copy' command to create an exact copy of your library. Here are the steps:
With a library open, choose Save a Copy from the File menu.
Choose where to save it.
Click Save.
The new library does not open, it is simply saved to disk.
Option Two
To use the Compressed Library command to save a copy of your library and.data folder together in a compressed file (.enlx) which can be restored later in EndNote.
From the File menu, select Compressed Library (.enlx) and then Create.
Select the folder or drive where you are saving which will then give you a Compressed EndNote Library (filename.enlx).

faqs.question: Why do author names change in EndNote?
faqs.answer:
If you are referencing a corporate author using EndNote, you need to put a comma at the end of the author so that EndNote recognises it as a corporate author and doesn't move any words around.
For example, referencing the author Department of Education in EndNote, it should be entered as:
Department of Education,
If there is already a comma in the name you need to put a second comma
E.g.
Department of Education, Northern Territory should be:
Department of Education,, Northern Territory
For more information, read this article from EndNote
If you have any concerns or other difficulties, contact us.

faqs.question: I am renting for the first time. What do I need to know?
faqs.answer:
Before looking at rentals/student accommodation make sure you do a budget on your income and expenses. Study Australia provide useful information on studying, working and living in Australia. There is also a Living Costs Calculator that can help with your preparations. Apart from the rent, there will be other household expenses, such as electricity, internet, food, phone, clothes, fuel, entertainment etc.
Once you have organised your budget and are sure of your weekly budget, check in with individual real estate agents, www.realestate.com.au, newspaper The NT News (Wednesdays and Saturday editions), CDU StudyStays, Gumtree, and various Facebook rental/lease breaks pages to look at your options for accommodation.

There's more detail on the page below.

faqs.question: Does the off-campus accommodation service check the property, the landlord and any people living in the property?
faqs.answer:
No - Accommodation Services do not check any properties listed on CDU StudyStays.
CDU Off-Campus Accommodation Officers can provide students with the resources to find and inspect properties independently. We can check your lease, application forms, and provide advice if you experience any tenancy problems. Unfortunately, we can’t find, inspect or submit applications for properties on your behalf, as it is important that you inspect the properties to find the one that is right for you.

Ask the Library or Student Central for the full details.

faqs.question: How do I find InPlace and book my placement or Sim Block?
faqs.answer:
Placements and Simulation Blocks (Sim Blocks) are managed in **InPlace**. Log in to the **CDU Portal**, open **My Apps** and choose **Placements (InPlace)**.

- InPlace updates within about **24 hours** of you enrolling in the placement or Sim Block unit. You'll then see a notification to book your spot.

- For anything else about your placement, contact the **placements team** for your course.

If Placements isn't in your My Apps list, contact **Student Central** on **1800 061 963**.

faqs.question: Do I have to attend classes live if I study online?
faqs.answer:
Most lectures and tutorials are **recorded**, so you can watch them later in **Learnline**. Open your unit and look under **Collaborate**.

For external (online) students, live attendance usually isn't compulsory. Some units do have required live sessions, though, so check your unit's Learnline site when it opens in O-Week.

If you can't make a class, let your **lecturer or unit coordinator** know.

faqs.question: Are my class times in Darwin time or my local time?
faqs.answer:
Timetables are published in **Darwin (NT) time**, but the Portal timetable and Learnline convert class times to **your computer's time zone**.

So if your computer is set to Queensland time, your timetable shows Queensland time. If you're unsure, check with your lecturer.

faqs.question: Why is my timetable empty or still changing?
faqs.answer:
Not all classes are confirmed early on. Timetables come out progressively and are all out **before Week 1**, and some units are still being finalised until then. Check your timetable about **once a week** for updates.

If it's still not appearing after you've followed the **New to CDU checklist**, and it's urgent, contact the **Timetable team**.

faqs.question: Why can't I see my units or their content in Learnline yet?

faqs.question: Am I studying full-time or part-time, and how many units should I take?
faqs.answer:
Usually **2 units or fewer** in a semester is **part-time**. A full-time load is more than that, typically **4 units** per semester.

To check your study load, log in to the **CDU Portal**, then go to **My Apps > MyStudentInfo > Enrolment**. You only need to enrol for the **upcoming semester**, not the whole year.

Study plans work for part-time study too. If you're not sure which units to pick, contact **Student Central** on **1800 061 963**.
